p.s: Going on a nice vacation with a relative and without a tour guide is the most relaxing vacation.
Traveling in a group has its postive and negative sides.
One of the negative sides is that people have to compromise to other people 's suggestions.
If a tourist travels alone or with a partner, they have the opportunity to go wherever they want and to do wantever they want.
To see a forgein country and its original culture, tourists have to step out of the box and leave the tour guide behind.
Going into a tiny village far away from tourism in which no tourists have been, is an adventure that speaks for itself.
Who want 's to see a place that has been seen by millions of other tourists?
My family and I went to Kenya, South Africa, and visited the tiny villages along the river.
We were the only tourist they had seen in years.
We saw the "real" life they are living and realized how greatful we should be for a life like ours.
This experience shows that not only will a vacation be memorable by seeing the hotel pool and hotel buffet but also by doing something exciting - something out of the box.
Considering the statement, I have to admit that it depends on age wheather tourists choose to travel in a group led by a tour guide.
It would be more amusing and exciting for older people to join a group since they like the company of other older people.
Older people would also enjoy the freedom of letting somebody else do the work - like a tour guide - and relax and enjoy their vacation.
At the end, it is a personal choice rather people wants to travel alone, with a partner, or with a group.
Every choice has its positive and negative aspects.
